subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What best describes 'one-off' production?
options: A single, often bespoke, product made to a specific requirement
Identical products made continuously 24 hours a day
Products made in set groups of the same item
Very large numbers of the same product on an assembly line
questions.explain: One-off (bespoke) production makes a single unique item, such as a made-to-measure piece of furniture.

questions.q: Which scale of production typically runs non-stop, 24 hours a day, seven days a week?
questions.explain: Continuous production runs without stopping to make materials such as chemicals, glass and aluminium efficiently.

questions.q: Why does mass production usually lower the unit cost of each product?
options: Fixed set-up costs are spread across a very large number of products
Each product is individually hand-finished by a skilled worker
Only expensive premium materials are used
Production stops frequently to change the tooling
questions.explain: High initial tooling and set-up costs are divided over huge output, reducing the cost per item.

questions.q: What is 'batch' production?
options: Making a specific quantity of identical products in a set group
Making one unique product to order
Making millions of identical products on a moving line
questions.explain: Batch production makes a defined number of the same item, and the line can be reset for a different batch afterwards.

questions.q: Why is batch production well suited to a business that makes several different seasonal products?
options: Equipment can be reset between batches to make different products
It removes the need for any tooling or set-up
It only ever produces a single item at a time
It always produces the lowest possible unit cost
questions.explain: Batch production offers flexibility because machines and tooling can be changed over to make a different product between batches.

questions.q: A workshop is asked to make 500 identical wooden stools for a school. Which scale of production is most appropriate?
questions.explain: A fixed, moderate quantity of identical items is a classic use of batch production.

questions.q: Which type of material is required for vacuum forming?
questions.explain: Vacuum forming softens a thermoplastic sheet with heat so it can be sucked down over a mould.

questions.q: Injection moulding shapes a product by:
options: Forcing molten polymer under pressure into a closed mould
Blowing air into a heated tube of polymer
Bending a sheet along a heated line
Bonding thin layers together with adhesive
questions.explain: Granules are melted and injected under high pressure into a mould cavity, then cooled to form the product.

questions.q: Why is blow moulding chosen to make plastic drinks bottles?
options: It can form thin-walled hollow containers
It produces very heavy solid components
It only works with thermosetting plastics
It is used to cut precise metal threads
questions.explain: Blow moulding inflates softened polymer against a mould to create hollow, thin-walled products such as bottles.

questions.q: Which of these is a permanent method of joining metal?
questions.explain: Welding fuses metals together to form a permanent joint that cannot be undone without damage.

questions.q: Which adhesive is most suitable for joining acrylic to acrylic?
questions.explain: Acrylic solvent cement chemically bonds acrylic parts by softening and fusing the surfaces.

questions.q: What happens during line bending (strip heating) of acrylic?
options: A localised strip is heated until soft so the sheet can be folded
The whole sheet is melted and poured into a mould
The sheet is cut using a rotating blade
The sheet is bonded to another using solvent
questions.explain: A strip heater warms a narrow line of thermoplastic so it can be bent to a chosen angle and held until cool.

questions.q: Why are knock-down (KD) fittings widely used in flat-pack furniture?
options: They allow furniture to be assembled and disassembled easily
They form a permanent, unopenable joint
They can only be used on solid hardwood
questions.explain: KD fittings let flat-pack furniture be quickly joined at home and taken apart again if needed.

questions.q: Laminating a material means:
options: Bonding thin layers together to build up strength or shape
Cutting a material into thin strips
Heating a material until it melts
Coating a metal in molten zinc
questions.explain: Laminating layers up thin sheets (or veneers) with adhesive, often around a former, to create strong curved shapes.

questions.q: A designer needs to mass-produce hollow plastic shampoo bottles. Which process is most suitable?
questions.explain: Blow moulding is the standard high-volume process for producing hollow plastic bottles.

questions.q: A cabinet maker needs a strong, interlocking corner joint for a drawer front. Which joint is most appropriate?
questions.explain: The interlocking pins and tails of a dovetail give a strong, attractive corner joint ideal for drawers.

questions.q: Galvanising protects steel by coating it with which metal?
questions.explain: Galvanising dips or coats steel in zinc to form a protective barrier that resists rusting.

questions.q: What is a try square mainly used for?
options: Marking and checking right angles (90 degrees)
questions.explain: A try square is used to mark and verify accurate 90-degree angles when marking out timber.

questions.q: Why is a finish such as paint or lacquer applied to a mild steel product?
options: To protect it from corrosion and improve appearance
To make the steel electrically conductive
To increase the melting point of the steel
questions.explain: Mild steel rusts readily, so a surface finish seals it from moisture and also enhances its appearance.

questions.q: A student must measure the diameter of a metal rod accurate to 0.01 mm. Which tool should they use?
questions.explain: A micrometer gives highly precise measurements, typically to 0.01 mm, ideal for small diameters.
